description: A French object relative clause with an embedded clause inside it: 19 words, 10 stages, 107 Replay steps, 71 final nodes and 217 relation marks. Before 19 October 2026 its offline preparation took about 12 seconds, most of it in the plaque schedule.
source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character spell-out contract (character-spellout-v3), 19 October 2026 (night4 batch, 13-fr-long-relative, analysis 1), commit bcf1b56. Tokens are the shared word list of that run.
sentence: Le livre que Marie pensait que Jean avait déjà lu se trouvait encore sur la table de la cuisine.

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines lu with the relative pronoun que as its internal argument. Déjà adjoins to this verbal constituent, and transitive v introduces Jean as the external argument. The resulting predicate assigns the theme role to que and the agent role to Jean; déjà takes scope over the reading event. The auxiliary avait, imperfect T, and the declarative complementizer que remain separate workspace objects. Labels identify the projecting lexical items or features, rather than additional X-bar levels. Inflected verbal forms enter with their lexical spelling; their tense dependencies will be established syntactically without decomposing those spellings.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the participial predicate and its initial argument structure.

values.interpretation: the reading precedes an embedded past reference time

derivationStages.stageRecord: First, Internal Merge moves the relative pronoun from the object position to the edge of transitive v, leaving a silent trace. This preserves an escape position before the lower phase is completed. Aux then selects the participial domain, and imperfect T selects the auxiliary projection. T agrees with Jean, licensing nominative Case, and Jean moves from its previously represented external-argument position to the subject position of T. A silent trace records that source. The perfect auxiliary locates the reading anterior to the embedded past reference time; its overt head remains below T at this stage.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the lower extraction edge, perfect structure, and embedded subject position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The auxiliary moves from its established position to T, yielding the finite auxiliary before déjà and lu. The abstract imperfect head remains silent inside the resulting head complex. Declarative que then selects the embedded T projection. The relative pronoun moves from the previously established v-edge to the edge of this C projection, leaving another silent trace. The two instances of que are distinct: the moving object pronoun and the stationary declarative complementizer. Only the former participates in the relative chain.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the embedded declarative clause and expose its relative-extraction edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The declarative clause becomes the propositional complement of pensait, and Marie is externally merged as the experiencer of that attitude predicate. Pensait is represented as a lexicalized v/V head: its lexical root and argument-introducing component are bundled, so the analysis does not posit a separate unrepresented V-to-v step. The embedded clause is a selected complement, not an adjunct island, and its relative pronoun remains accessible at the C-edge. A second imperfect T and a silent relative C are introduced as separate objects for the next operations.
derivationStages.statement: Build the selecting predicate pensait with Marie as its external argument.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative pronoun moves from the embedded C-edge to an outer edge of the v projection headed by pensait. Its former C-edge position becomes a silent trace, preserving the successive-cyclic path through the selected clause. Imperfect T merges above this domain, agrees with Marie, and attracts Marie from its earlier external-argument position to the subject position. Pensait itself remains in its base head position until the next stage.
derivationStages.statement: Pass the relative dependency through the attitude predicate and raise Marie.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Pensait raises from its established lexicalized v/V position to imperfect T. Silent relative C selects that finite clause. The relative pronoun then moves from the attitude-v edge to the relative C-edge, leaving its final intermediate trace. The pronounced que is therefore the highest occurrence of an object dependency whose thematic source is the complement of lu, not an argument of pensait. The chain is represented with silent traces rather than fully articulated lower copies; only its highest occurrence is pronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the finite relative clause and its long-distance object chain.

values.analysis: external nominal head with a matching relative operator
values.interpretation: books that Marie thought Jean had already read
the table associated with the kitchen

derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative clause adjoins to the nominal projection of livre, and Le closes the resulting definite description. The relative operator is interpreted with livre as its external antecedent; this is a matching-style external-head analysis, not movement of the pronounced noun out of the relative clause. Separately, de la cuisine attaches inside the nominal projection of table, identifying the kitchen-associated table. La closes that nominal, and sur takes the resulting DP as its ground. Thus de la cuisine modifies table, not livre or the attitude predicate.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the definite antecedent and the internally modified locative phrase.

values.interpretation: the book is located on the table
encore applies to the locative state

derivationStages.stageRecord: The locative PP combines with trouvait, represented as a lexicalized nonagentive v/V head. The book DP is merged as the sole thematic subject of this pronominal locative predicate. Encore adjoins to the locative verbal projection, taking scope over the state of the book's being on the table. Its continuative and possible repetitive interpretations do not require distinct attachment structures here. Se is introduced as the pronominal voice clitic of se trouver: it is not a second, referential object and does not assign the book a reflexive agent–patient interpretation. Main-clause imperfect T merges above the clitic projection. Both the subject and trouvait remain in their lower positions at this stage.
derivationStages.statement: Build the pronominal locative predicate with its theme subject and encore.

values.piedPiping: the restrictive relative remains inside the moving subject

derivationStages.stageRecord: Main T agrees with the entire book DP and licenses its nominative Case. The DP moves from its previously represented thematic position to the subject position of T, carrying its restrictive relative clause with it; a silent DP trace remains below. Trouvait then raises from its lexicalized v/V position to T. Se is a deficient clitic head rather than an intervening verbal head, so this analysis does not require an additional verbal landing there. The verb now precedes encore, while se remains in its earlier clitic position pending attachment to the finite head.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the main subject and establish the finite locative verb.

values.placement: se precedes the finite verb trouvait

derivationStages.stageRecord: Se moves from its previously represented clitic position and left-adjoins to the finite T complex containing trouvait. Its source becomes a silent clitic trace, giving the pronounced order se trouvait encore. A silent declarative C closes the main clause without triggering further movement. The completed tree pronounces the external nominal head and its relative clause in the subject, the highest relative pronoun before Marie, and the separate embedded complementizer before Jean. All movement traces and abstract functional heads remain silent. The pronounced terminals consequently yield exactly the input sentence; no special realization associations are needed.
derivationStages.statement: Attach the proclitic and complete the declarative sentence.
